docs.title: CoWork Demo Creator
docs.text:
spn-demo-creator is a Cortex Code skill that builds a complete Snowflake CoWork demo for you:

  • synthetic data with a story built into it
  • a semantic view for structured questions
  • a Cortex Search service for documents
  • a Cortex Agent that uses both
  • six demo questions and a timed demo script

It works in two modes:

Mode Use it when Industry You have no named customer yet, or you are running a workshop. The skill researches the industry and proposes three use cases. Customer You have a named customer. The skill researches the company and tailors the use cases.

docs.title: The demo story
docs.text:
Every demo follows the same three acts, so it lands in about ten minutes.

  1. What happened: a headline number with a clear split.
  2. Rule out the obvious: the thing everyone suspects turns out not to matter.
  3. Find the real drivers: the agent finds the hidden patterns, backs them with documents, and recommends what to do.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
1. Prerequisites
  2. Install the skill
  3. Follow the step by step guide
  4. Run the demo

Unofficial

This is a community skill for Snowflake partners. It is not supported by Snowflake. All data it creates is synthetic.

docs.title: How a question is answered
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Agent
    participant Analyst as Cortex Analyst
    participant Search as Cortex Search
    User->>Agent: Why are we losing in this segment?
    Agent->>Analyst: Break the metric down by segment and time
    Analyst-->>Agent: Rows and a chart
    Agent->>Search: Find documents about that segment
    Search-->>Agent: Matching passages
    Agent-->>User: Answer with charts and cited evidence

docs.title: Approval gates
docs.text: The skill stops and asks you at five points so nothing is built that you have not approved: audience brief, use case, data model, data patterns, and the final demo script.

docs.title: One-time account setup
docs.text:
Run sql/00_setup.sql as ACCOUNTADMIN. It creates:

  • database COWORK_DEMOS
  • warehouse COWORK_DEMO_WH
  • notification integration COWORK_DEMO_EMAIL
  • procedure COWORK_DEMOS.PUBLIC.SEND_MAIL

Use your own names if you prefer, and tell the skill when it asks.

docs.title: Install the skill
docs.text:
1. Clone the repo:

    git clone https://github.com/sfc-gh-makukreja/spn-demo-creator.git

  2. Copy the folder into your Cortex Code skills folder:

    cp -R spn-demo-creator ~/.snowflake/cortex/skills/spn-demo-creator

  3. Open Cortex Code and connect to the account you set up.

  4. Ask for a demo:

    Create a CoWork demo for the retail industry

    or

    Create a CoWork demo for https://www.example.com

docs.title: Run the demo
docs.text:
About ten minutes.

  1. Open Snowsight: AI & ML > Agents and choose your agent.
  2. Warm it up with one question ten minutes before.
  3. Follow the demo script. Ask the six questions in order.
  4. Keep the fallback screenshots ready.

docs.title: The story
docs.text: Act Question type What the audience sees 1 What The headline number and its split 2 Why The obvious cause does not explain it 3 Why and how The real drivers, document evidence, a recommendation and an action

docs.title: Clean up
docs.text: Run sql/99_teardown.sql after replacing the names.

docs.title: Adding screenshots
docs.text:
Each step page has a slot for a screenshot.

  1. Save the image in docs/assets/img/ using the name shown on the page, for example 04-schema.png.

  2. In the page, replace the "Screenshot to add" block with:

    ![Create the schema](../assets/img/04-schema.png)

  3. Preview locally:

    python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install mkdocs mkdocs-material
.venv/bin/mkdocs serve

Use PNG, crop to the relevant area, and blur anything that is not synthetic (account names, emails).

docs.title: Semantic view creation fails
docs.text:
• Metrics must not have data_type.
  • Use SYSTEM$CREATE_SEMANTIC_VIEW_FROM_YAML, not CREATE SEMANTIC VIEW ... FROM @stage.
  • Tables used in relationships need a primary_key.
  • Check that tables and columns exist.

docs.title: Search service not active
docs.text:
• Check the warehouse.
  • Check the text column is not NULL.
  • Wait two to three minutes for indexing.

docs.title: Agent creation fails
docs.text:
• Valid tool types are cortex_analyst_text_to_sql, cortex_search, data_to_chart, web_search and generic.
  • Custom tools need type, execution_environment and identifier.
  • Check cross-region inference is on.

docs.title: Agent does not respond
docs.text:
• Test each tool alone.
  • Check the role has USAGE on the agent.

docs.title: Email fails
docs.text:
• The recipient must be a verified email address in the account.
  • The integration and procedure must exist (sql/00_setup.sql).

docs.title: Data looks unrealistic or the story is missing
docs.text:
• Re-run the pattern checks and adjust the thresholds.
  • Use normal or Poisson distributions and keep patterns subtle.

Tip

Snowflake syntax changes. If a statement fails, check the current documentation.

docs.text:
The skill has eleven steps and five approval stops.

Step What Stop 0 Choose the mode 1 Research confirm summary 2 Audience approve brief 3 Use case approve use case 4 Create the schema 5 Design the data model approve model 6 Generate the data review pattern checks 7 Semantic view 8 Cortex Search 9 Cortex Agent 10 Sample questions 11 Demo script review script

docs.text: Goal: Decide whether the demo is for an industry or a named customer.

docs.title: What happens
docs.text: The skill asks one question: customer or industry? Industry mode skips company and people research. Customer mode asks for the company website.

docs.title: What you do
docs.text: Create a CoWork demo for the industry

docs.title: Output

docs.title: 1. Research
docs.text: Goal: Understand the industry or customer well enough to propose realistic use cases.

docs.title: What happens
docs.text: The skill uses web search to gather trends, data-intensive processes, pain points and typical personas (industry mode), or the company overview, products, news and competitors (customer mode). It summarizes the findings and asks you to confirm or correct them.

docs.title: What you do
docs.text: Confirm the summary, or correct anything that is wrong.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: A context summary you have approved.

docs.title: 2. Audience
docs.text: Goal: Tailor the demo to the people in the room.

docs.title: What happens
docs.text: The skill asks about the audience. In industry mode you describe roles only. In customer mode you may name attendees, and the skill uses only public professional information. It presents a short brief: priorities, likely pain points, level of detail, what to avoid. Stop: approve the brief.

docs.title: What you do
docs.text: The room is partner SEs and solution architects.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: An approved audience brief.

docs.title: 3. Use case
docs.text: Goal: Pick one use case that covers both structured and unstructured data.

docs.title: What happens
docs.text: Either bring your own use case or ask the skill for three options. Each option has a business problem, a structured angle, an unstructured angle, why it resonates, and target personas. The skill then summarises the chosen use case as lists of structured, unstructured and combined questions. Stop: approve it.

docs.title: 5. Design the data model
docs.text: Goal: Design tables that can tell the story.

docs.title: What happens
docs.text: First the skill writes the story contract: the headline split, the dimension to rule out, and the real drivers with target rates. Then it designs 4 to 6 structured tables and 1 or 2 document tables, with helper columns and filterable metadata. Stop: approve the data model.

docs.title: What you do
docs.text: Approve the model.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Approved table designs and the story contract.

docs.title: 6. Generate the data
docs.text: Goal: Create realistic data with the story built in.

docs.title: What happens
docs.text: The skill creates tables in dependency order and loads dimensions before facts. Driver columns use one random roll per row and thresholds per segment so the target rates hold. It then runs one verification query per act and compares to the targets. Stop: review the results.

docs.title: What you do
docs.text: Looks right, continue.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Populated tables and verified patterns.

docs.title: What happens
